# Monitoring Runner

The Apify actor [`apify/monitoring-runner`](https://apify.com/apify/monitoring-runner) as typed Telo kinds, generated from its build **0.0.217**. The module's version is that build number, and every run it starts is pinned to exactly that build, so the input types below are the ones the actor really runs with.

The monitoring runner is a part of the Apify Monitoring Suite (apify/monitoring). See its readme for more information and how to use this.

## Pricing

Free — you pay only for the Apify platform usage (compute units) of the run.

Runs are charged to the Apify account whose token the `ApifyClient` holds. See the [Store page](https://apify.com/apify/monitoring-runner) for current prices.

## Import

```yaml
imports:
  Actor: oci://ghcr.io/telorun/apify/apify-monitoring-runner@0.0.217#sha256-…
```

Pin the digest with `telo upgrade`. The module re-exports `ApifyClient`, so it is the only import needed.

## Usage

```yaml
kind: Actor.ApifyClient
metadata: { name: apify }
token: !cel "secrets.apifyToken"
---
kind: Actor.Run          # or Actor.Start for runs longer than 5 minutes
metadata: { name: scrape }
client: !ref apify
maxTotalChargeUsd: 1     # optional: timeout, memory, maxItems, maxTotalChargeUsd
---
kind: Run.Sequence
metadata: { name: main }
steps:
  - name: scrape
    invoke: !ref scrape
    inputs:
      targetType: "ACTOR"
```

- **`Run`** calls Apify's synchronous endpoint and returns `{ items }`. Apify holds the request open for at most 300 seconds; a longer run fails with HTTP 408.
- **`Start`** starts the run, long-polls it until it finishes, and returns `{ run, items }`. A run that ends `FAILED`, `TIMED-OUT` or `ABORTED` raises `APIFY_RUN_NOT_SUCCEEDED` with the run as `data`.

## Input

Only these fields are accepted — `telo check` rejects any other.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `projectName` | string |  |  | Monitoring suite name — Name of your monitoring suite. It will be used in notifications and to identify related resources in the Apify dashboard. |
| `targetType` | string | yes | `"ACTOR"` | Type of target — Only one type of target can be monitored by a single monitoring suite. If you want to watch more types, create more monitoring suites. |
| `targetPatternList` | array |  | `[]` | Target name patterns — Regular expressions that will be matched against selected actors / tasks or datasets under your Apify account. All matching targets will then be monitored by this monitoring suite. This is typically also the fastest way to select a single target. Just type its full name. Datas |
| `targetList` | array |  | `[]` | Target IDs — If for whatever reason the Target name pattern option does not suit you, targets can also be specified by providing their IDs, as found in your Apify dashboard. |
| `limit` | integer |  | `1000` | Max items to be checked — Last items to be checked. If 100 is passed, only last hundred runs/datasets will be checked. |
| `saveHistory` | boolean |  | `false` | Save history — All monitoring runs results are saved in named dataset |
| `resourceStatsCollector` | boolean |  |  | Resource stats collector — Works with Subject type 'Actor', 'Task' and 'Named dateaset', Gets information about the runs TODO: LINK TO PA |

| `checkersInput` | object |  |  | Checkers input — Pass input to checkers |

| `emailReporter` | boolean |  |  | Email — Sends report to mail inbox. LINK TO PA for input |
| `slackReporter` | boolean |  |  | Slack — Sends report to custom slack channel. LINK TO PA for input |

## Output

The actor publishes no dataset schema, so `items` are untyped objects.
